clips.title: From horse trainer to AI agency owner
clips.speaker: Ty
clips.hook_q: Can you start an agency with zero experience?
clips.notes: VERIFY agency name (transcript says 'Black Throwing Co').
clips.transcript: My name is Ty. I am 25 from Dallas. I own Black Throwing Co. I started it from, started after COVID once I got out of the horse training industry. I'm a little depressed after that, so I needed something that kind of gave my life more purpose, more meaning, something I kind of keep going through. And then out came Black Throwing Co, a digital marketing and automation agency, where we build websites, build AI agents, as well as, you know, one -on -one ads and create content.

clips.title: Watching others post made her brave enough to
clips.speaker: intern (green)
clips.hook_q: Scared to post your first video?
clips.transcript: I think like my saving grace was really the community that I felt within the internship. Being around a lot of like -minded people, we're all going to do the same thing. We're all struggling with the same things. And we all kind of have like the same fear and anxieties in a lot of ways. So being able to see someone else put themselves out there kind of encouraged me and made me feel better about putting myself out there so they could do, there's no reason why I couldn't do it.

clips.title: One sentence of advice for young founders
clips.speaker: Andrew + interns
clips.hook_q: One sentence of advice for young founders?
clips.transcript: If you had one piece of advice and you can give someone one sentence, well, especially young people our age, you know, trying to start a business, what would it be for me? Don't you start with you, Ty? Just do it. Agreed. I would say get yourself out there, be curious, do hard things and just do the acceptable things. So yeah, same thing, but honestly, 1 % better every day. Just do one small thing that's going to make you better every single day. And that's going to make you that's going to stack up.

clips.title: Successful people failed a thousand times
clips.speaker: McKinley
clips.hook_q: What do successful people do differently?
clips.hook_plain: They failed 1,000 times. Then kept going.
clips.transcript: the people that are successful in life, they failed a thousand times, but they kept going. That's why they are. When you fail, you quit. But if you never fail, you will eventually get no matter what. I think doing hard things more often too, you get very accustomed to being uncomfortable and getting through it, even though it sucks.

clips.title: 21, still in college, running an AI consulting company
clips.speaker: Ohaji
clips.hook_q: Can you run an AI company while in college?
clips.hook_plain: 21. Senior at Ohio State. AI company.
clips.transcript: So I'm Ohaji 21 from Columbus, Ohio, senior at Ohio State University. And the way that I got started into this was my mom, she's a serial entrepreneur, has a couple of businesses, so I always wanted to go into that venture. I just didn't know what avenue. Obviously, coming from a tech background, I knew I wanted to go into something tech -related, and AI kind of was that avenue. So I started in the past year with ET Solutions, AI Consulting, and that kind of blew up from there.

clips.title: Meet HighLevel's 2026 interns
clips.speaker: Andrew + Ty + McKinley + Ohaji
clips.notes: Intro montage (Andrew asked for it). The 4th intern doesn't introduce themself in this edit.
clips.transcript: Hey, what's up, high -levelers? My name is Andrew. I'm here with the high -level interns from 2026. They're going to tell you a little bit about their businesses, their advice for getting started with high -level, and yeah, let's just jump right into it. … So, Ty, tell me a little bit about yourself. My name is Ty. I am 25 from Dallas. … McKinley, tell me a little bit about yourself. Yeah, so I started a YouTube channel back when I was like 10 years old and kind of got started into marketing in that way. … Ohaji? So I'm Ohaji 21 from Columbus, Ohio, senior at Ohio State University.

clips.title: Started an agency in high school. Felt like an outcast.
clips.speaker: McKinley
clips.hook_plain: Agency at 16. Zero friends who got it.
clips.transcript: I think I started my agency back in high school and was very much, I wouldn't say made fun of, but a little bit of an outcast when it comes to your typical friend group. They're not into business, they're not into marketing, they don't really do content creation or anything like that. It's definitely been kind of a lonely route in some portions of business.

clips.title: If you're gonna fail, fail forward
clips.speaker: Ty
clips.hook_q: What's the right way to fail?
clips.transcript: if you're gonna fail, fail forward, if you're gonna fall, fall forward, always try to, you know, stumble a little bit further than what you were yesterday. Yeah. And I think that's one of the things the internship really did, you know, put instill in us. Resilience and determination was a huge takeaway.
